Revenue Accountant
Accounting & Finance · Berlin, Germany

Own the revenue & AR engine of a scaling energy-tech company, where clean accounting directly enables growth, trust, and Series-B-readiness.
trawa enables mid-sized companies to access green, intelligent energy. Our business sits at the intersection of energy flows, complex B2B contracts, and fast-moving markets, which makes our revenue anything but standard: energy products, variable pricing, and multiple billing cadences, each with its own recognition logic and data source.
As our Revenue Accountant, you will own the processes that turn this complexity into clean, auditable numbers. You'll work closely with our Tech and Data team on 15-minute interval energy data, hundreds of contract variants, and data flowing from CRM, energy warehouse, and finance tooling into a single revenue truth. A lot of what you'll need doesn't exist yet, you'll help build it from the ground up.
This is a role for someone who wants real ownership in a small, fast-growing team, and who is looking for a company they can grow with as we scale toward Series B and beyond.
What You'll Own
Revenue Recognition & Contract Accounting
Apply and maintain revenue recognition policies (HGB today, IFRS 15 on the horizon) across trawa's customer and contract types
Translate commercial terms (variable pricing, multi-element arrangements, energy-specific structures) into the right accounting treatment
Own and reconcile deferred revenue and energy accrual schedules
Customer Billing & Accounts Receivable
Co-own a defined scope of the invoicing process end-to-end, from creation through reconciliation
Drive AR reconciliations and aging; own dunning and collections
Month-End Close, Reporting & Audit Readiness
Own revenue-related close activities: journal entries, account reconciliations, variance commentary
Maintain audit-ready workpapers and documentation for all revenue and AR positions
Proactively flag policy gaps and propose fixes, before the auditor does
IT & Finance Transformation
Contribute to our Billing Tool Rollout and ERP selection as the revenue voice
Help replace manual workflows with automations, you don't just flag inefficiencies, you fix them
Your First 90 Days
Month 1 - Learn the Landscape: Build an understanding of trawa's business model, revenue processes, and accounting workflows, while taking ownership of recurring tasks such as invoice tracking, reconciliations, and AR reviews.
Month 2 - Take Ownership: Independently manage key revenue accounting activities, contribute to the month-end close, and identify opportunities to improve billing, reconciliation, or revenue recognition processes.
Month 3 - Build and Improve: Own assigned close activities end-to-end, deliver audit-ready documentation, and drive one structural improvement to revenue reporting or process automation.

3-5 years in accounting, with meaningful exposure to complex revenue accounting, AR, or billing, ideally in a B2B SaaS, energy, or tech-enabled business
Solid accounting fundamentals with hands-on experience in IFRS 15 or HGB revenue recognition in a contract-heavy environment, comfortable with deferred revenue and month-end close
Ownership mindset: you don't wait to be told what's broken, you find it, fix it, and document it
Analytical and data-curious: comfortable with large datasets, spotting anomalies, forming a hypothesis and testing it against the data before escalating
Structured and detail-oriented: your reconciliations are clean, your documentation holds up under audit scrutiny
Proficient in Excel / Google Sheets
Business fluent in German and English

AI-first mindset: hands-on with tools like Langdock, Claude, ChatGPT, or n8n, you've built workflows, not just used chat. Bonus if you've built your own automations.
SQL or Python basics (or willingness to learn quickly) to query billing and energy data directly
Experience with DATEV, Moss, Airtable , or ERP implementations
Exposure to energy billing, commodity contracts, or variable pricing structures
Experience supporting or preparing for an external audit
Don't worry if you don't match every box, we value drive and learning speed over perfect CVs

Real ownership from day one, you'll run processes that directly affect the quality of our financial reporting and customer relationships
A uniquely complex business model at the intersection of energy, software, and B2B contracts
An AI-first Finance team that embraces new tools and ways of working, we automate first, hire second
Direct collaboration with Finance leadership and cross-functional leaders from day one
Accelerated career growth in a scaling environment where your scope grows with the business
Flexible working, 30 vacation days, L&D budget, competitive compensation, meal vouchers, Urban Sports membership, and a vibrant Berlin office culture

We work with multiple businesses and clients, which means our accounting team operates in a multi-company environment . Our Accounting Managers aren't responsible for just one set of books, one leadership team, or one monthly close. They are managing multiple clients, priorities, deadlines, accounting systems, and stakeholders at the same time.

That environment requires more than strong accounting fundamentals. It requires organization, judgment, communication, ownership, and the ability to keep a lot of moving pieces moving in the right direction.

Position Overview We’re looking for an Accounting Manager who can own the accounting function across multiple assigned clients while leading and developing Staff Accountants. This is a hands-on accounting leadership role.

You’ll oversee day-to-day accounting activity, review Staff Accountant work, manage month-end close, review financial statements, maintain accounting controls, identify issues, and work closely with Controllers to ensure they have accurate and reliable financial information.

Experience managing accounting for multiple companies at once is extremely important for this role. The ideal candidate has worked in a fractional accounting, outsourced accounting, public accounting, CAS, accounting firm, or similar multi-client environment where managing several sets of books simultaneously was part of the normal workflow.

You should be comfortable jumping between different businesses, accounting systems, stakeholders, deadlines, and financial situations without losing the plot. Basically: if you like one set of books, one close calendar, and one predictable workflow, this probably isn't your dream job. You SHOULD Apply If
You have experience managing accounting for multiple companies or clients simultaneously

You take ownership when something goes wrong and focus on solving the problem rather than assigning blame
You SHOULD NOT Apply If
Your experience has been exclusively within a single company's accounting department and you've never managed multiple companies or clients at once
You need a highly predictable workload with one set of books and one consistent workflow
You prefer purely transactional accounting and don't enjoy reviewing or developing other accountants

Job Summary: As a Sr. Staff Accountant at Creative Chaos , you will play a crucial role in our finance team by performing various accounting and financial tasks. You will be responsible for maintaining accurate financial records, preparing financial reports, and assisting with the overall financial management of the company. Duties & Responsibilities:

Recording Financial Transactions: Accurately record day-to-day banking and credit card transactions in financial books, ensuring that all entries are complete and error-free.

Bank Reconciliations: Perform regular bank reconciliations to ensure that our financial records match the bank statements, identifying and resolving any discrepancies promptly.

Accounts Payable and Receivable: Record bills and invoices, and ensure they are processed promptly. Additionally, maintain a record of outstanding customer invoices and vendor bills.

General Journal Entries: Enter general journal entries as needed to capture any financial transactions that do not fit into the standard categories.

Vendor and Customer Statement Reconciliation: Reconcile vendor and customer statements to ensure that our records align with external statements, addressing any discrepancies.

Month-End Accruals: Record month-end accruals accurately to reflect outstanding expenses or revenues for the period, ensuring our financial statements are up-to-date.

Payroll Processing : Assist in recording and processing payroll transactions

Prepaid Expense Schedules: Prepare and maintain prepaid expense schedules to accurately reflect the prepaid expenses on the balance sheet.

Fixed Assets Register: Maintain an up-to-date fixed assets register, tracking the value and depreciation of the tangible assets.

Inventory Reconciliation: Reconcile inventory records with physical counts and make necessary adjustments to maintain accurate inventory valuations.

1099 Reporting: Generate 1099 data for review

Experience with QuickBooks or other similar accounting software is a plus.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

The Role We are seeking a Senior Accounting Manager to serve as a key strategic partner to the Controller, architecting our global accounting policies and driving large-scale finance transformations. You will act as the bridge between technical GAAP and business strategy, owning the end-to-end integrity of our global inventory and COGS.

This role is designed for a leader who looks beyond the current close to build the systems and policies required for a global, public-scale organization. What You’ll Do End-to-End Ownership
Own inventory accounting and COGS globally, including month-end close, reconciliations, variance analysis, reporting, and audit support.
Own judgment-based inventory estimates, including excess & obsolete (E&O) and warranty reserves, including methodology design, assumptions, governance, documentation, and final review/sign-off in compliance with U.S. GAAP.
Serve as the final decision-maker for inventory accounting policy, methodologies, and judgment-based estimates, ensuring consistent application and governance across the organization.
Strategic & Cross-Functional Leadership
Partner cross-functionally with Supply Chain, Operations, Product, FP&A, and Finance Systems to align financial outcomes with operational realities and inform business decisions.
Lead COGS and gross margin analysis, translating financial results into clear insights and actions for leadership and stakeholders.
Act as a finance partner to non-finance teams, translating inventory and cost accounting concepts into clear, actionable insights.
Process, Systems & Scale
Own the finance transformation roadmap related to inventory accounting, including future-state process design, system architecture, and automation strategy; partner with Finance Systems and cross-functional stakeholders to scale inventory accounting through ERP optimization, data integrity, and workflow automation.
Own inventory capitalization and COGS allocation frameworks, ensuring consistent application of accounting policy as the company scales.
Actively participate in modifying and updating ŌURA’s ASC 705 Cost of Sales and Services policy to reflect the company's changing needs.
Drive operational efficiency and scalability by simplifying, standardizing, and automating inventory accounting workflows.
Controls, Audit & Risk Management
Strengthen inventory-related internal controls, physical inventory processes, and audit readiness, including SOX-aligned documentation and control design.
Lead the relationship with external auditors for all inventory and COGS matters, serving as the primary subject matter expert for technical accounting positions and complex audit inquiries.
People Leadership & Change Management
Lead, mentor, and develop the accounting team, including goal setting, performance management, coaching, and succession planning.
Act as a change leader and thought partner, designing and implementing future-state inventory accounting processes and operating models.
Provide leadership support to the Accounting organization on ad-hoc initiatives, complex problem solving, and strategic priorities, bringing a holistic view across policy, systems, controls, and business impact.

Degree: A degree (Bachelors or higher) in accounting; or a degree (Bachelors or higher) in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting. Wir verstehen die Halbleiterindustrie als ein Universum voller Möglichkeiten. Wir erkennen Chancen und sehen das transformative Potenzial, das unsere Graphen-Lösungen für die Neugestaltung der Branche mit sich bringen.
Wir laden Sie ein, diesen Wandel gemeinsam mit uns voranzutreiben, indem wir kluge Köpfe mit einer gemeinsamen Vision zusammenbringen. Diese Vision ist es, zu zeigen, dass grundlegende Veränderungen möglich sind. Mit Ihrem Wissen und Ihren Fähigkeiten können Sie beweisen, dass Dinge anders – und besser – gemacht werden können.
Gemeinsam haben wir die Kraft, das Paradigma zu verändern, wie die Welt vernetzt ist.

Die steigenden Anforderungen der Halbleiterindustrie an leistungsfähigere Chips mit höherer Bandbreite und geringerem Energieverbrauch werden durch unsere Technologie adressiert. Wir ermöglichen die Verbindung von Chips mit Hochdurchsatz-Computernetzwerken bei minimaler Latenz.
